summary.name: Training Site Reliability Engineers (Google SRE)
summary.one_liner: A Google SRE book-site article on designing training programs for Site Reliability Engineers based on organization maturity, infrastructure knowledge, and engineer experience.
use_cases: Designing an SRE training program for a company
Deciding what training new SREs need
Tailoring SRE courses to team maturity
Planning onboarding for engineers moving into SRE roles
Assessing engineers' gaps in SRE skills and infrastructure knowledge
summary.what_it_does: The page is a written article from Google's SRE team about training Site Reliability Engineers. It argues that training needs vary by three factors: how mature the organization is in adopting SRE principles, practices and culture; how much the individuals know about the organization and its infrastructure; and how experienced they are in technical skill and familiarity with the SRE model. It presents these as dimensions to explore when designing a learning program. The text shown is only the introduction; the detailed course design guidance is not present in the provided text.
notable: Written by Google SRE team members (Jennifer Petoff, JC van Winkel, Preston Yoshioka and others)
Frames SRE training around three variables: organization maturity, infrastructure knowledge, and engineer experience
Part of Google's public SRE resources; listed in the awesome-sre Education section
caveats: Only the introduction is in the provided text; the full course-design details are not shown
Guidance is general and conceptual rather than a ready-made curriculum
